Summary: US01: A secure file transfer connection to the vendor
Description: As the IT Integration Lead, I want a secure file transfer connection to the vendor, so that customer data is protected in transit.
Acceptance Criteria: Encrypted SFTP connection tested both ways; keys stored in the bank vault; Information Security approves.

Summary: US02: Every daily transaction extracted from core banking
Description: As an AML analyst, I want every daily transaction extracted from core banking, so that nothing escapes monitoring.
Acceptance Criteria: Extract covers cash, cheques, EFTs and wires; runs nightly; file lands by 4:00 a.m. CST.

Summary: US03: Transaction fields mapped to our data model
Description: As the vendor, I want transaction fields mapped to our data model, so that scenarios read the right values.
Acceptance Criteria: Mapping document signed off by IT and AML Ops; all mandatory fields mapped.

Summary: US04: Customer KYC and risk rating data loaded
Description: As an AML analyst, I want customer KYC and risk rating data loaded, so that alerts reflect who the customer is.
Acceptance Criteria: Customer type, occupation, risk rating and expected activity loaded daily.

Summary: US05: A data quality profiling report
Description: As the AML Ops Manager, I want a data quality profiling report, so that we know where data gaps will cause false alerts.
Acceptance Criteria: Report shows completeness for every mandatory field; gaps over 1% flagged.

Summary: US06: Record counts reconciled on every load
Description: As Internal Audit, I want record counts reconciled on every load, so that I can prove all transactions were monitored.
Acceptance Criteria: Counts and totals match core banking at 100%; any break raises an alert to IT.

Summary: US07: The daily load fully automated
Description: As an AML analyst, I want the daily load fully automated, so that alerts are ready when I start work.
Acceptance Criteria: Load completes by 6:00 a.m. CST on 10 consecutive test days.

Summary: US30: Failed loads to retry and notify us
Description: As IT Support, I want failed loads to retry and notify us, so that problems are fixed before analysts arrive.
Acceptance Criteria: Automatic retry once; on second failure email and page on call support.

Summary: US31: A load monitoring view
Description: As IT Support, I want a load monitoring view, so that I can see each day's status at a glance.
Acceptance Criteria: Shows load time, record count and status for the last 30 days.

Summary: US32: Incomplete customer records cleansed
Description: As the KYC team, I want incomplete customer records cleansed, so that profile based scenarios work.
Acceptance Criteria: Records missing occupation or risk rating reduced from 3.2% to under 0.5%.

Summary: US10: Structuring detected
Description: As an AML analyst, I want structuring detected, so that I can spot customers splitting cash to avoid reporting.
Acceptance Criteria: Alert when 2 or more cash deposits of $9,000 to $9,999 each occur within 5 days; passes test cases TC01 to TC04.

Summary: US11: Large cash transactions flagged
Description: As a compliance reporting officer, I want large cash transactions flagged, so that LCTRs are never missed.
Acceptance Criteria: Flags $10,000 or more in cash within a 24 hour period, single or combined; passes TC05 to TC07.

Summary: US33: A scenario test data set
Description: As the test lead, I want a scenario test data set, so that every scenario can be tested repeatably.
Acceptance Criteria: Synthetic data set with known expected alerts for every scenario.

Summary: US34: Scenario thresholds editable with approval
Description: As the AML Ops Manager, I want scenario thresholds editable with approval, so that we can tune without vendor help.
Acceptance Criteria: Threshold change needs CCO approval in system; every change logged.

Summary: US12: Wires to or from high risk jurisdictions flagged
Description: As an AML analyst, I want wires to or from high risk jurisdictions flagged, so that I can review cross border risk.
Acceptance Criteria: Flags wires involving countries on the bank's high risk list; passes TC08 to TC10.

Summary: US13: Rapid movement of funds detected
Description: As an AML analyst, I want rapid movement of funds detected, so that I can spot pass through accounts.
Acceptance Criteria: Flags when 80% or more of incoming funds leave within 48 hours, over $5,000; passes TC11 to TC13.

Summary: US35: To maintain the high risk country list
Description: As the AML Ops Manager, I want to maintain the high risk country list, so that it stays current.
Acceptance Criteria: List editable by authorized users only; changes logged.

Summary: US36: Each alert risk scored
Description: As an AML analyst, I want each alert risk scored, so that I work the riskiest alerts first.
Acceptance Criteria: Score from 1 to 100 based on scenario, amount and customer risk rating.

Summary: US14: Activity inconsistent with the customer profile flagged
Description: As an AML analyst, I want activity inconsistent with the customer profile flagged, so that unusual behaviour stands out.
Acceptance Criteria: Flags monthly activity over 3 times expected activity; passes TC14 to TC16.

Summary: US15: Dormant accounts that suddenly reactivate flagged
Description: As an AML analyst, I want dormant accounts that suddenly reactivate flagged, so that I can check for account takeover or misuse.
Acceptance Criteria: Flags accounts inactive 12 months or more with over $5,000 activity in 30 days; passes TC17 to TC18.

Summary: US37: Expected activity fields from KYC used in scoring
Description: As an AML analyst, I want expected activity fields from KYC used in scoring, so that profile alerts are accurate.
Acceptance Criteria: Expected monthly volume and value loaded and used by US14.

Summary: US08a: Interac e-Transfer data designed into the feed (CR001)
Description: As an AML analyst, I want Interac e-Transfer data designed into the feed (CR001), so that e-Transfers are monitored.
Acceptance Criteria: Data source, mapping and extract design approved.

Summary: US08b: Interac e-Transfer data loaded daily (CR001)
Description: As an AML analyst, I want Interac e-Transfer data loaded daily (CR001), so that no transaction type is missed.
Acceptance Criteria: e-Transfers included in daily load and reconciliation at 100%.

Summary: US16: An alert queue sorted by risk score
Description: As an AML analyst, I want an alert queue sorted by risk score, so that I always know what to work next.
Acceptance Criteria: Queue filters by scenario, score, age and analyst.

Summary: US17: To investigate and close alerts with a written rationale
Description: As an AML analyst, I want to investigate and close alerts with a written rationale, so that every decision is documented.
Acceptance Criteria: Alert cannot close without rationale of at least 50 characters and a disposition code.

Summary: US18: To approve analyst decisions (maker/checker)
Description: As a team lead, I want to approve analyst decisions (maker/checker), so that no alert is closed by one person alone.
Acceptance Criteria: Analyst cannot approve own work; team lead approval required for every closure.

Summary: US19: To attach documents and notes to a case
Description: As an AML analyst, I want to attach documents and notes to a case, so that all evidence is in one place.
Acceptance Criteria: Upload PDF, image and email files up to 20 MB each.

Summary: US20: To escalate an alert to an STR case
Description: As an AML analyst, I want to escalate an alert to an STR case, so that suspicious activity is reported.
Acceptance Criteria: Escalation creates STR case linked to all related alerts.

Summary: US21: An STR draft generated from case data
Description: As a compliance reporting officer, I want an STR draft generated from case data, so that reports are fast and complete.
Acceptance Criteria: All mandatory FINTRAC STR fields populated or flagged as missing.

Summary: US22: LCTR drafts with a due date tracker
Description: As a compliance reporting officer, I want LCTR drafts with a due date tracker, so that every LCTR is filed within 15 calendar days.
Acceptance Criteria: Draft generated next day; tracker warns at day 10 and day 13.

Summary: US23: Role based access
Description: As Information Security, I want role based access, so that people see only what their job needs.
Acceptance Criteria: Roles: analyst, team lead, manager, auditor (read only), admin; approved by InfoSec.

Summary: US24: Every user action logged
Description: As Internal Audit, I want every user action logged, so that I can reconstruct any decision.
Acceptance Criteria: Log shows who, what, when for every view, edit, approval; cannot be edited.

Summary: US25: Records kept for at least five years
Description: As the CCO, I want records kept for at least five years, so that we meet PCMLTFA record keeping rules.
Acceptance Criteria: Retention rule set to 5 years from case closure; deletion only after expiry.

Summary: US38: Vendor support during the penetration test
Description: As Information Security, I want vendor support during the penetration test, so that findings are understood quickly.
Acceptance Criteria: Test completed; findings logged in Jira.

Summary: US09: 13 months of history loaded
Description: As an AML analyst, I want 13 months of history loaded, so that profile and dormancy scenarios work from day one.
Acceptance Criteria: 13 months loaded and reconciled.

Summary: US26: Penetration test findings fixed
Description: As Information Security, I want penetration test findings fixed, so that the system is safe to go live.
Acceptance Criteria: Both medium findings fixed and retested.

Summary: US27: A dashboard of alert volumes, ageing and false positive rate
Description: As the AML Ops Manager, I want a dashboard of alert volumes, ageing and false positive rate, so that I can manage workload.
Acceptance Criteria: Dashboard refreshes daily; drill down by scenario and analyst.

Summary: US29: A training sandbox with sample data
Description: As the Training Lead, I want a training sandbox with sample data, so that analysts can practise safely.
Acceptance Criteria: Sandbox with masked data available to all 27 users.

Summary: US28: Board level trend reports
Description: As the CCO, I want board level trend reports, so that I can report AML performance to the board.
Acceptance Criteria: Monthly trend report by scenario. Deferred to post go live under CR001.
